sanskrit: brahmovāca rajo 'haṃ vaḥ pravakṣyāmi yāthātathyena sattamāḥ nibodhata mahābhāgā guṇavṛttaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Brahmā said: I shall now declare to you rajas as it truly is, O most excellent ones; give heed, O greatly fortunate, to the working of this quality in all its forms.

sanskrit: saṃghāto rūpam āyāsaḥ sukhaduḥkhe himātapau aiśvaryaṃ vigrahaḥ saṃdhir hetuvādo 'ratiḥ kṣamā
english: Aggregation, form, exertion, pleasure and pain, cold and heat, lordship, conflict, treaty-making, disputation, discontent, forbearance —

sanskrit: balaṃ śauryaṃ mado roṣo vyāyāmakalahāv api īrṣyepsā paiśunaṃ yuddhaṃ mamatvaṃ paripālanam
english: strength, valour, intoxication, fury, toil and quarrel as well, envy, craving, slander, war, possessiveness, protection,

sanskrit: vadhabandhaparikleśāḥ krayo vikraya eva ca nikṛnta chindhi bhindhīti paramarmāvakartanam
english: killing, binding, and torment, buying and selling too, and the cutting at another's vital points with cries of 'cut, slash, split!' —

sanskrit: ugraṃ dāruṇam ākrośaḥ paravittānuśāsanam lokacintā vicintā ca matsaraḥ paribhāṣaṇam
english: the cruel and the harsh, abuse, the directing of others' wealth, worldly anxiety and brooding, spite, and reproachful speech,

sanskrit: mṛṣāvādo mṛṣādānaṃ vikalpaḥ paribhāṣaṇam nindā stutiḥ praśaṃsā ca pratāpaḥ paritarpaṇam
english: false speech and false giving, doubt and contention, blame, praise and eulogy, fierce splendour, gratification,

sanskrit: paricaryā ca śuśrūṣā sevā tṛṣṇā vyapāśrayaḥ vyūho 'nayaḥ pramādaś ca paritāpaḥ parigrahaḥ
english: attendance and the wish to serve, service, thirst, dependence, marshalling of forces, misrule, heedlessness, affliction, and acquisition,

sanskrit: saṃskārā ye ca loke 'smin pravartante pṛthak pṛthak nṛṣu nārīṣu bhūteṣu dravyeṣu śaraṇeṣu ca
english: and whatever rites and dispositions arise in this world, severally, among men, among women, among creatures, in goods, and in refuges,

sanskrit: saṃtāpo 'pratyayaś caiva vratāni niyamāś ca ye pradānam āśīryuktaṃ ca satataṃ me bhavatv iti
english: distress and distrust, and those vows and observances, and the giving joined with the prayer 'let this ever be mine' —

sanskrit: svadhākāro namaskāraḥ svāhākāro vaṣaṭkriyā yājanādhyāpane cobhe tathaivāhuḥ parigraham
english: the utterance of svadhā, salutation, the utterance of svāhā, the vaṣaṭ-rite, and both the officiating at sacrifice and the teaching of it, and likewise acceptance of fees — these too they call rajas.

sanskrit: idaṃ me syād idaṃ me syāt sneho guṇasamudbhavaḥ abhidrohas tathā māyā nikṛtir māna eva ca
english: 'Let this be mine, let this be mine' — attachment born of the qualities, and treachery, and illusion, deceit, and pride as well,

sanskrit: stainyaṃ hiṃsā parīvādaḥ paritāpaḥ prajāgaraḥ stambho dambho 'tha rāgaś ca bhaktiḥ prītiḥ pramodanam
english: theft, injury, calumny, anguish, sleeplessness, stubbornness and hypocrisy, and passion, devotion, fondness, and merriment,

sanskrit: dyūtaṃ ca janavādaś ca saṃbandhāḥ strīkṛtāś ca ye nṛttavāditragītāni prasaṅgā ye ca ke cana sarva ete guṇā viprā rājasāḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ
english: gambling and gossip, and the ties contracted through women, dancing, instrumental music, and song, and whatever attachments there be — all these, O brāhmaṇas, are proclaimed to be qualities of rajas.

sanskrit: bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyāṇāṃ bhāvānāṃ bhuvi bhāvanāḥ trivarganiratā nityaṃ dharmo 'rthaḥ kāma ity api
english: The strivings on earth after things past, present, and to come, ever bent upon the threefold aim — dharma, artha, and kāma —

sanskrit: kāmavṛttāḥ pramodante sarvakāmasamṛddhibhiḥ arvāksrotasa ity ete taijasā rajasāvṛtāḥ
english: those who follow desire rejoice in the abundance of every desire; these are the downward-flowing, the fiery ones, enveloped by rajas.

sanskrit: asmiṃl loke pramodante jāyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ pretyabhāvikam īhanta iha laukikam eva ca dadati pratigṛhṇanti japanty atha ca juhvati
english: In this world they take their joy, being born again and again; they strive both for the fruit that follows death and for what belongs to this world; they give and receive, they mutter prayers and they pour oblations.

sanskrit: rajoguṇā vo bahudhānukīrtitā; yathāvad uktaṃ guṇavṛttam eva ca naro hi yo veda guṇān imān sadā; sa rājasaiḥ sarvaguṇair vimucyate
english: The qualities of rajas have been recounted to you in their many forms, and the working of the quality told as it is; for the man who ever knows these qualities is freed from all the qualities of rajas.

sanskrit: brahmovāca ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi tṛtīyaṃ guṇam uttamam sarvabhūtahitaṃ loke satāṃ dharmam aninditam
english: Brahmā said: Next I shall declare the third and highest quality, the good of all beings in the world, the blameless law of the virtuous.

sanskrit: ānandaḥ prītir udrekaḥ prākāśyaṃ sukham eva ca akārpaṇyam asaṃrambhaḥ saṃtoṣaḥ śraddadhānatā
english: Bliss, delight, exaltation, luminous clarity, and happiness too, generosity, freedom from agitation, contentment, faithfulness,

sanskrit: kṣamā dhṛtir ahiṃsā ca samatā satyam ārjavam akrodhaś cānasūyā ca śaucaṃ dākṣyaṃ parākramaḥ
english: forbearance, steadfastness, and non-injury, evenness, truth, uprightness, freedom from anger and from envy, purity, skill, and prowess —

sanskrit: mudhā jñānaṃ mudhā vṛttaṃ mudhā sevā mudhā śramaḥ evaṃ yo yuktadharmaḥ syāt so 'mutrānantyam aśnute
english: knowledge held free of self-interest, conduct free of it, service free of it, toil free of it — he who is thus disciplined in duty attains the infinite in the world beyond.

sanskrit: nirmamo nirahaṃkāro nirāśīḥ sarvataḥ samaḥ akāmahata ity eṣa satāṃ dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Free of 'mine,' free of ego, free of expectation, even-minded toward all, unstricken by desire — this is the eternal law of the virtuous.

sanskrit: viśrambho hrīs titikṣā ca tyāgaḥ śaucam atandritā ānṛśaṃsyam asaṃmoho dayā bhūteṣv apaiśunam
english: Trust, modesty, and endurance, renunciation, purity, vigilance, kindliness, freedom from delusion, compassion toward beings, freedom from slander,

sanskrit: harṣas tuṣṭir vismayaś ca vinayaḥ sādhuvṛttatā śāntikarma viśuddhiś ca śubhā buddhir vimocanam
english: gladness, satisfaction, and wonder, humility, good conduct, works of peace and inner cleansing, an auspicious mind, and deliverance,

sanskrit: upekṣā brahmacaryaṃ ca parityāgaś ca sarvaśaḥ nirmamatvam anāśīstvam aparikrītadharmatā
english: equanimity and chastity, and renunciation utter and complete, freedom from 'mine,' freedom from expectation, the practice of duty unbought —

sanskrit: mudhā dānaṃ mudhā yajño mudhādhītaṃ mudhā vratam mudhā pratigrahaś caiva mudhā dharmo mudhā tapaḥ
english: giving free of self-interest, sacrifice free of it, study free of it, vow free of it, acceptance of gifts free of it, duty free of it, austerity free of it.

sanskrit: evaṃvṛttās tu ye ke cil loke 'smin sattvasaṃśrayāḥ brāhmaṇā brahmayonisthās te dhīrāḥ sādhudarśinaḥ
english: Whoever in this world walk thus, taking their stand in sattva — those brāhmaṇas, abiding in the source that is Brahman, are the steadfast, the seers of the good.

sanskrit: hitvā sarvāṇi pāpāni niḥśokā hy ajarāmarāḥ divaṃ prāpya tu te dhīrāḥ kurvate vai tatas tataḥ
english: Having cast off all sins, free of sorrow, ageless and deathless, those steadfast ones, attaining heaven, then work their will here and there.

sanskrit: īśitvaṃ ca vaśitvaṃ ca laghutvaṃ manasaś ca te vikurvate mahātmāno devās tridivagā iva
english: Sovereignty and mastery and the swiftness of mind — these the great-souled ones bring forth at will, like the gods who roam the triple heaven.

sanskrit: ūrdhvasrotasa ity ete devā vaikārikāḥ smṛtāḥ vikurvate prakṛtyā vai divaṃ prāptās tatas tataḥ yad yad icchanti tat sarvaṃ bhajante vibhajanti ca
english: These are remembered as the upward-flowing, the gods born of modification; having reached heaven, they transform things by their very nature, here and there; whatever they desire, all that they enjoy and apportion.

sanskrit: ity etat sāttvikaṃ vṛttaṃ kathitaṃ vo dvijarṣabhāḥ etad vijñāya vidhival labhate yad yad icchati
english: Thus has the conduct of sattva been told to you, O bulls among the twice-born; knowing this duly, one obtains whatever he desires.

sanskrit: prakīrtitāḥ sattvaguṇā viśeṣato; yathāvad uktaṃ guṇavṛttam eva ca naras tu yo veda guṇān imān sadā; guṇān sa bhuṅkte na guṇaiḥ sa bhujyate
english: The qualities of sattva have been proclaimed in detail, and the working of the quality told as it is; the man who ever knows these qualities enjoys the qualities, and is not himself devoured by them.

sanskrit: brahmovāca naiva śakyā guṇā vaktuṃ pṛthaktveneha sarvaśaḥ avicchinnāni dṛśyante rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamas tathā
english: Brahmā said: The qualities cannot be told here as wholly distinct from one another; rajas, sattva, and tamas are seen unbroken, blent together.

sanskrit: anyonyam anuṣajjante anyonyaṃ cānujīvinaḥ anyonyāpāśrayāḥ sarve tathānyonyānuvartinaḥ
english: They cleave to one another, they live upon one another, all of them lean upon one another and follow after one another.

sanskrit: yāvat sattvaṃ tamas tāvad vartate nātra saṃśayaḥ yāvat tamaś ca sattvaṃ ca rajas tāvad ihocyate
english: As far as sattva extends, so far tamas is present — of this there is no doubt; and as far as tamas and sattva reach, so far, it is said here, reaches rajas.

sanskrit: saṃhatya kurvate yātrāṃ sahitāḥ saṃghacāriṇaḥ saṃghātavṛttayo hy ete vartante hetvahetubhiḥ
english: Joined together they make their journey, traveling in company; for these act as an aggregate and proceed by causes and non-causes.

sanskrit: udrekavyatirekāṇāṃ teṣām anyonyavartinām vartate tad yathānyūnaṃ vyatiriktaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Among these that abide in one another, in their predominance and their excess, the relation holds throughout, now lesser, now greater.

sanskrit: vyatiriktaṃ tamo yatra tiryagbhāvagataṃ bhavet alpaṃ tatra rajo jñeyaṃ sattvaṃ cālpataraṃ tataḥ
english: Where tamas is in excess, sinking to the state of the lower creatures, there rajas is to be known as scant, and sattva scantier still.

sanskrit: udriktaṃ ca rajo yatra madhyasrotogataṃ bhavet alpaṃ tatra tamo jñeyaṃ sattvaṃ cālpataraṃ tataḥ
english: And where rajas is in excess, moving in the middle current, there tamas is to be known as scant, and sattva scantier still.

sanskrit: udriktaṃ ca yadā sattvam ūrdhvasrotogataṃ bhavet alpaṃ tatra rajo jñeyaṃ tamaś cālpataraṃ tataḥ
english: And when sattva is in excess, flowing in the upward current, there rajas is to be known as scant, and tamas scantier still.

sanskrit: sattvaṃ vaikārikaṃ yonir indriyāṇāṃ prakāśikā na hi sattvāt paro bhāvaḥ kaś cid anyo vidhīyate
english: Sattva is the source of modification, the illuminator of the senses; no other state whatever is ordained as higher than sattva.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ jaghanyaguṇasaṃyuktā yānty adhas tāmasā janāḥ
english: Those grounded in sattva go upward, those of rajas remain in the middle, and the men of tamas, yoked to the lowest quality, go downward.

sanskrit: tamaḥ śūdre rajaḥ kṣatre brāhmaṇe sattvam uttamam ity evaṃ triṣu varṇeṣu vivartante guṇās trayaḥ
english: Tamas in the śūdra, rajas in the kṣatriya, and supreme sattva in the brāhmaṇa — thus do the three qualities revolve among the three classes.

sanskrit: dūrād api hi dṛśyante sahitāḥ saṃghacāriṇaḥ tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajaś caiva pṛthaktvaṃ nānuśuśruma
english: Even from afar they are seen together, traveling in company — tamas, sattva, and rajas; we have never heard of their being apart.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā cādityam udyantaṃ kucorāṇāṃ bhayaṃ bhavet adhvagāḥ paritapyeraṃs tṛṣṇārtā duḥkhabhāginaḥ
english: At the sight of the rising sun, fear comes to wicked thieves, while travelers are scorched, afflicted with thirst and overtaken by distress.

sanskrit: ādityaḥ sattvam uddiṣṭaṃ kucorās tu yathā tamaḥ paritāpo 'dhvagānāṃ ca rājaso guṇa ucyate
english: The sun is taken to be sattva, the base thieves are as tamas, and the scorching of the travelers is called the quality of rajas.

sanskrit: prākāśyaṃ sattvam āditye saṃtāpo rājaso guṇaḥ upaplavas tu vijñeyas tāmasas tasya parvasu
english: In the sun, its radiance is sattva, its burning the quality of rajas; but its eclipse, at the conjunctions, is to be known as the tāmasa quality.

sanskrit: evaṃ jyotiḥṣu sarveṣu vivartante guṇās trayaḥ paryāyeṇa ca vartante tatra tatra tathā tathā
english: Thus in all the heavenly lights the three qualities revolve, and they hold sway by turns, in this place and that, in this way and that.

sanskrit: sthāvareṣu ca bhūteṣu tiryagbhāvagataṃ tamaḥ rājasās tu vivartante snehabhāvas tu sāttvikaḥ
english: And in immobile beings, tamas, sunk to the state of the lower order, and rajas qualities revolve there too; but the oily, nurturing essence is sāttvika.

sanskrit: ahas tridhā tu vijñeyaṃ tridhā rātrir vidhīyate māsārdhamāsavarṣāṇi ṛtavaḥ saṃdhayas tathā
english: The day is to be known as threefold, and the night is ordained as threefold; so too months, fortnights, and years, the seasons, and the junctures of time.

sanskrit: tridhā dānāni dīyante tridhā yajñaḥ pravartate tridhā lokās tridhā vedās tridhā vidyās tridhā gatiḥ
english: Threefold are the gifts that are given, threefold the sacrifice proceeds; threefold the worlds, threefold the Vedas, threefold the sciences, threefold the course of beings.

sanskrit: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyac ca dharmo 'rthaḥ kāma ity api prāṇāpānāv udānaś cāpy eta eva trayo guṇāḥ
english: Past, present, and to come; dharma, artha, and kāma as well; the prāṇa, the apāna, and the udāna — these too are the three qualities.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cid iha vai loke sarvam eṣv eva tat triṣu trayo guṇāḥ pravartante avyaktā nityam eva tu sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva guṇasargaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Whatever there is in this world, all of it rests in these three; the three qualities, ever unmanifest, hold sway — sattva, rajas, and tamas, the eternal creation of the qualities.

sanskrit: tamo 'vyaktaṃ śivaṃ nityam ajaṃ yoniḥ sanātanaḥ prakṛtir vikāraḥ pralayaḥ pradhānaṃ prabhavāpyayau
english: Tamas is the unmanifest, the auspicious, the eternal, the unborn, the everlasting womb — Nature, modification, dissolution, the primal matter, origin and end.

sanskrit: anudriktam anūnaṃ ca hy akampam acalaṃ dhruvam sad asac caiva tat sarvam avyaktaṃ triguṇaṃ smṛtam jñeyāni nāmadheyāni narair adhyātmacintakaiḥ
english: Without excess and without lack, unshaking, unmoving, fixed, both being and non-being — all this unmanifest is remembered as having the three qualities; these are the names to be known by men who ponder the inner self.

sanskrit: avyaktanāmāni guṇāṃś ca tattvato; yo veda sarvāṇi gatīś ca kevalāḥ vimuktadehaḥ pravibhāgatattvavit; sa mucyate sarvaguṇair nirāmayaḥ
english: He who truly knows the names of the unmanifest and the qualities, and all the courses of beings in their pure essence — freed from the body, knowing the truth of their distinction — he, made whole, is released from all the qualities.

sanskrit: brahmovāca avyaktāt pūrvam utpanno mahān ātmā mahāmatiḥ ādir guṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prathamaḥ sarga ucyate
english: Brahmā said: From the unmanifest there arose first the Great Self, of mighty intellect, the beginning of all the qualities; it is called the first creation.

sanskrit: mahān ātmā matir viṣṇur viśvaḥ śaṃbhuś ca vīryavān buddhiḥ prajñopalabdhiś ca tathā khyātir dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ
english: The Great Self, Mind, Viṣṇu, the All, the mighty Śambhu, intellect, wisdom, perception, and likewise fame, steadfastness, memory —

sanskrit: paryāyavācakaiḥ śabdair mahān ātmā vibhāvyate taṃ jānan brāhmaṇo vidvān na pramohaṃ nigacchati
english: by these synonymous names the Great Self is made manifest; the learned brāhmaṇa who knows it falls not into delusion.

sanskrit: sarvataḥpāṇipādaś ca sarvatokṣiśiromukhaḥ sarvataḥśrutimāṃl loke sarvaṃ vyāpya sa tiṣṭhati
english: With hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads, and faces on every side, with ears on every side, he stands in the world, pervading all.

sanskrit: mahāprabhārciḥ puruṣaḥ sarvasya hṛdi niśritaḥ aṇimā laghimā prāptir īśāno jyotir avyayaḥ
english: The Person, whose flame is of mighty splendour, lodged in the heart of all — minuteness, lightness, attainment, the Lord, the imperishable light.

sanskrit: tatra buddhimatāṃ lokāḥ saṃnyāsaniratāś ca ye dhyānino nityayogāś ca satyasaṃdhā jitendriyāḥ
english: There are the worlds of the wise, of those devoted to renunciation, the meditators, ever-yoked, true to their word, their senses conquered,

sanskrit: jñānavantaś ca ye ke cid alubdhā jitamanyavaḥ prasannamanaso dhīrā nirmamā nirahaṃkṛtāḥ vimuktāḥ sarva evaite mahattvam upayānti vai
english: and whoever are endowed with knowledge, free of greed, their wrath subdued, of tranquil mind, steadfast, free of 'mine,' free of ego, all liberated — these indeed attain to greatness.

sanskrit: ātmano mahato veda yaḥ puṇyāṃ gatim uttamām sa dhīraḥ sarvalokeṣu na moham adhigacchati viṣṇur evādisargeṣu svayaṃbhūr bhavati prabhuḥ
english: He who knows the holy and supreme course of the Great Self, that steadfast one comes to no delusion in any of the worlds; for in the primal creations it is Viṣṇu who becomes the self-existent Lord.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi yo veda guhāśayaṃ prabhuṃ; naraḥ purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ viśvarūpam hiraṇmayaṃ buddhimatāṃ parāṃ gatiṃ; sa buddhimān buddhim atītya tiṣṭhati
english: The man who thus knows the Lord seated in the secret heart, the ancient Person of cosmic form, golden, the supreme goal of the wise — that wise one, transcending the intellect, abides beyond it.

sanskrit: brahmovāca ya utpanno mahān pūrvam ahaṃkāraḥ sa ucyate aham ity eva saṃbhūto dvitīyaḥ sarga ucyate
english: Brahmā said: That Great One who arose first is then called the I-maker; coming into being as 'I,' it is called the second creation.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāraś ca bhūtādir vaikārika iti smṛtaḥ tejasaś cetanā dhātuḥ prajāsargaḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: The I-maker, the origin of the elements, is remembered as the modifying principle; it is the conscious essence of energy, the begetter of creatures, the Lord of beings.

sanskrit: devānāṃ prabhavo devo manasaś ca trilokakṛt aham ity eva tat sarvam abhimantā sa ucyate
english: It is the source of the gods, the god, and of the mind; the maker of the three worlds; it is called the one that conceives all this as 'I.'

sanskrit: adhyātmajñānanityānāṃ munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām svādhyāyakratusiddhānām eṣa lokaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: For the sages ever devoted to the knowledge of the inner self, their souls refined, perfected through study and sacrifice, this is the eternal world.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāreṇāharato guṇān imān; bhūtādir evaṃ sṛjate sa bhūtakṛt vaikārikaḥ sarvam idaṃ viceṣṭate; svatejasā rañjayate jagat tathā
english: Drawing these qualities together by the I-maker, the origin of the elements thus creates, the maker of beings; the modifying principle sets all this in motion, and so colours the world with its own radiance.

sanskrit: brahmovāca ahaṃkārāt prasūtāni mahābhūtāni pañca vai pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam
english: Brahmā said: From the I-maker were born the five great elements — earth, air, ether, water, and fire as the fifth.

sanskrit: teṣu bhūtāni muhyante mahābhūteṣu pañcasu śabdasparśanarūpeṣu rasagandhakriyāsu ca
english: In these five great elements creatures are bewildered — in sound, touch, and form, and in taste, smell, and action.

sanskrit: mahābhūtavināśānte pralaye pratyupasthite sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ dhīrā mahad utpadyate bhayam
english: When the destruction of the great elements draws near and dissolution is at hand, a mighty terror arises in all that bears the breath of life; but the steadfast remain unmoved.

sanskrit: yady asmāj jāyate bhūtaṃ tatra tat pravilīyate līyante pratilomāni jāyante cottarottaram
english: If a being is born from this, into that it again dissolves; they dissolve in reverse order and are born each from the one before.

sanskrit: tataḥ pralīne sarvasmin bhūte sthāvarajaṅgame smṛtimantas tadā dhīrā na līyante kadā cana
english: Then, when all beings, the moving and the unmoving, have dissolved away, the steadfast, possessed of true memory, are never dissolved at all.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśas tathā rūpaṃ raso gandhaś ca pañcamaḥ kriyākāraṇayuktāḥ syur anityā mohasaṃjñitāḥ
english: Sound, touch, and form, taste, and smell as the fifth, joined with action and cause, are impermanent and known as the marks of delusion.

sanskrit: lobhaprajanasaṃyuktā nirviśeṣā hy akiṃcanāḥ māṃsaśoṇitasaṃghātā anyonyasyopajīvinaḥ
english: Bound up with greed and procreation, without distinction, owning nothing, mere aggregates of flesh and blood, living upon one another —

sanskrit: bahir ātmāna ity ete dīnāḥ kṛpaṇavṛttayaḥ prāṇāpānāv udānaś ca samāno vyāna eva ca
english: these are the outer self, wretched, of pitiable conduct; the prāṇa and apāna, the udāna, the samāna, and the vyāna as well —

sanskrit: antarātmeti cāpy ete niyatāḥ pañca vāyavaḥ vāṅmanobuddhir ity ebhiḥ sārdham aṣṭātmakaṃ jagat
english: these are the inner self, the five fixed breaths; together with these — speech, mind, and intellect — the world is of eightfold nature.

sanskrit: tvagghrāṇaśrotracakṣūṃṣi rasanaṃ vāk ca saṃyatā viśuddhaṃ ca mano yasya buddhiś cāvyabhicāriṇī
english: He whose skin, nose, ears, and eyes, whose tongue and speech are restrained, whose mind is wholly pure and whose intellect never strays —
